name: file-audit
description: Map fan-out audit: a shell node lists files matching a glob as a PathManifest whose entries are 'path|content-fingerprint' (so per-item caching invalidates when file CONTENT changes, not just the path list); one auditor per file emits Finding[]; an arbiter gate adjudicates the collected findings into a Verdict; a report node summarizes. NOTE: the map node is readonly for parallel fan-out - the executor stanza must declare readonly_argv (remove "readonly" on bare pi; audits then serialize).

args.focus: correctness, staleness vs the code or data the file describes, broken references, contradictions with neighboring files

cmd:
import sys, json, hashlib, subprocess, fnmatch, pathlib
pattern = sys.argv[1]
cap = int(sys.argv[2])
out = subprocess.run(['git', '-c', 'core.quotepath=off', 'ls-files', '-z'], capture_output=True, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
if out.returncode != 0:
    sys.stderr.write('git ls-files failed: ' + (out.stderr or ''))
    sys.exit(1)
matched = [f for f in out.stdout.split('\x00') if f.strip() and fnmatch.fnmatch(f, pattern)]
files = matched[:cap]
entries = []
for f in files:
    try:
        h = hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(f).read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
    except OSError as e:
        h = 'unreadable'
    entries.append(f + '|' + h)
notes = '%d of %d matching files' % (len(files), len(matched))
if len(matched) > cap:
    notes += ' (TRUNCATED - raise --arg max_files to widen)'
print(json.dumps({'schema_version': '1.0', 'files': entries, 'notes': notes}))

spec.task:
Per-file auditors reviewed a set of files independently. Their raw findings follow as data (an array of Finding arrays, one per audited file; if the value spilled to a file, read that file):
{steps.audit.json}

Adjudicate: flatten and deduplicate; spot-check each blocker/major claim against the actual file before upholding it; discard unfounded or trivial findings. Emit one Verdict: verdict "block" if any upheld finding is a blocker, otherwise "pass" (majors are reported but do not block an audit). Put ONLY upheld findings in the findings array (same Finding shape) and give a one-sentence reason including how many files were audited.

Your result MUST be ONLY the Verdict JSON object: findings (array), verdict ("pass" or "block"), reason (string).

cmd:
import sys, json
v = sys.argv[1]
try:
    v = json.loads(v)
except ValueError:
    pass
print('file-audit verdict: ' + str(v))
